chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ismail, all together, from Hanaan ibn Sadeer, who said:

A woman was with us in Al-Hayy, and she had a slave girl who was a lamenter. She came to my father and said, 'O uncle, you know that my livelihood is from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and then from this slave girl, the lamenter. I would like you to ask Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about that. If it is permissible, (fine); otherwise, I will sell her and eat from her price until Allah brings relief.' My father said to her, 'By Allah, I consider it a significant matter that I should ask Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about this question.'

He said, 'So when we proceeded to him, I informed him with that. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Does she stipulate (a price beforehand)?' I said, 'By Allah, I do not know whether she stipulates or not.' He said: 'Tell her not to stipulate, and she can accept whatever is given.'

key_terms.تُشَارِطُ: She stipulates (a specific price or condition beforehand)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a slave girl who works as a lamenter according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the fiqh of *naihah* (professional lamenting) by addressing the specific mechanism of selling a slave girl engaged in this trade. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises against stipulating a fixed price (*tashir*) beforehand, preferring an open acceptance of whatever is offered, which reflects the scholarly view that the earnings are permissible despite the act being disliked or prohibited for the slave herself. This ruling highlights the distinction between the validity of the transaction and the moral status of the profession in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Ismail altogether, from Hanaan Bin Sadeyr who said,

‘There was a woman with us in Al-Hayy, and for her is a slave girl, a lamenter. So she came over to my father and said, ‘O uncle! You know that my livelihood is from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, then from this slave girl, the lamenter, and I would love it if you could ask Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about that. So if it was Permissible (fine), or else I would sell her and eat from her price until such time as Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Grants me with the relief (alternative source of income)’. So my father said to her, ‘I consider it a big thing that I should ask Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about this question’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So when we proceded to him<sup>asws</sup>, I informed him<sup>asws</sup> with that, so Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Does she stipulate (a price beforehand)?’ I said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I do not know whether she stipulates or not’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Tell her not to stipulate, and she can accept whatever is given’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il all from Hanan ibn Sadir who has said

the following: “In our neighborhood there was a woman who had a slave-girl who sang eulogies. She came to my father and said, ‘O Uncle, you know about my means of living from Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, and then it is from this slave-girl’s singing eulogies. I like if you ask abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, for me about it if it is lawful; otherwise, I will sell her and use the funds from selling her until Allah opens up a door for me.’ My father said to her, ‘I consider abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, greatly exalted and cannot ask such things from him.’

He (the narrator) has said that when we visited him (the Imam) I informed him (the Imam) about it and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, asked, ‘Does she set a condition?’ I replied, ‘By Allah, I do not know if she does or does not do.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Tell her not to set up a condition for payment but accept whatever is given to you.’”
